bkn: A single-binary backend core: namespaced document collections, typed settings, identity, and sandboxed scripts over embedded SQLite, driven entirely from the CLI.
one_liner: bkn gives a project the two primitives every backend re-invents - a place to put documents and a place to put settings - as one static binary with no database server, no runtime, and no admin UI. Every capability is a CLI verb first and an HTTP route second.

model.single binary: The tool is the server, the client and the migration runner. There is nothing else to install and no container to build.
model.single writer: bkn owns its SQLite file. Consumers reach it through the CLI or the HTTP API, never by opening the database themselves. This is the rule that keeps the data model changeable.
model.two primitives: store holds documents in namespaced collections; kv holds typed settings; auth holds users, organizations and tokens; script runs sandboxed JavaScript over all of them. Features are built on top of these, not added beside them.
model.namespaces: Every collection is addressed as <namespace>/<collection>. The namespace is the owning app, so two apps never collide and no caller has to guess a table name.
model.cli is the api: Any verb available over HTTP is available as a subcommand with the same shape. Agents drive the CLI; browsers and services drive the HTTP routes.
model.scripts are userland: Anything that is a scheduled HTTP call, a transform over stored records, or a webhook handler is a script, not a core feature. This is what keeps the core small enough to change.
model.identity is not billing: auth carries no subscription, plan or Stripe fields. In the system bkn replaces they lived on the user record, and the missing endpoint to write one is what drove a consumer to bypass the API and write the database directly. Billing belongs in a store collection, managed by a script.

loop: bkn guide - read this, once, to learn the model
bkn help-json - discover the exact commands, flags and exit codes
bkn store put myapp/users --data '{"email":"A@B.io"}' - write a document; the collection is created on first write
bkn store find myapp/users --where email=a@b.io - read it back by any field
bkn kv set myapp.stripe_key sk_live_... --type encrypted - store a secret sealed with the active key
bkn script test --file draft.js --input '{}' - try a script before storing it
bkn script create digest --file draft.js - store it, then run it by name or over HTTP
bkn serve - expose the same primitives over HTTP when a service needs them
bkn daemon start - background that server and poll it healthy

concepts.ref: A collection address, '<namespace>/<collection>'. Both segments are lowercase, start with a letter, and may contain digits, '-' and '_'.
concepts.document: A JSON object. Its id is returned merged in under the 'id' key, so reads give one flat object rather than a wrapper.
concepts.id: 26-char sortable ULID, minted by bkn unless you supply one - pass --id, or include 'id' in the document body. Ids are immutable; patch cannot change one.
concepts.normalizer: A per-collection rule ('lower', 'upper', 'trim', 'trim_lower') declared on a field. bkn applies it on every write AND to every filter value for that field, so a lookup always finds what a write stored.
concepts.filter: A single field equality predicate, 'field=value'. Values that parse as a number, true, false or null are compared as that type.
concepts.kv type: 'string' (opaque), 'json' (validated on write), or 'encrypted' (sealed with AES-256-GCM before storage, opened on read).
concepts.keyring: The set of keys that can decrypt, plus the one id that encrypts. Rotation means adding a key, pointing BKN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_ID at it, and running 'bkn kv rekey'.
concepts.public entry: A kv entry marked --public is readable through the unauthenticated HTTP settings route. An encrypted entry can never be public.
concepts.script: A stored JavaScript program that must define a top-level function main(input). Its return value is the run's result. It gets store, kv and allow-listed outbound HTTP, and nothing else - no filesystem, no processes, no timers, no require.
concepts.allow_net: The per-script list of hostnames bkn.http.fetch may reach ('api.stripe.com', or '*.example.com'). Empty means no network. Connections that resolve to a private or loopback address are refused regardless, unless BKN_SCRIPT_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NET=1.
concepts.run: One execution, recorded with its status (ok|error|timeout), input, result, logs and duration. Read them back with 'bkn script runs <name>'.
concepts.user: A global identity with an email (always normalized), a bcrypt password hash, and a platform role of user or admin. The platform role governs the deployment, not any tenant.
concepts.organization: A tenant, addressed by slug. Users join one through a membership that carries an org role: owner > admin > member.
concepts.access token: A short-lived (15m) HS256 JWT carrying sub, email, role, org and org_role. It cannot be revoked, which is why it is short - use 'auth me' to resolve it against the live user record.
concepts.refresh token: A long-lived (30d) opaque token, stored only as a digest and single-use: every refresh rotates it. Revocable via 'auth logout' or 'auth revoke'.

gotchas: The data file is ~/.bkn/bkn.db unless BKN_DATA says otherwise. There is exactly one resolution rule - never hardcode a path in a consumer.
patch is a shallow merge. A nested object in the patch replaces the stored one wholesale; it is not deep-merged.
store list defaults to 50 records. Pass --limit explicitly when you mean 'all', and page with --offset.
kv list never returns the value of an encrypted entry - it comes back empty. Fetch encrypted values one at a time with kv get.
Without an encryption key configured, 'kv set --type encrypted' fails loudly. It will never fall back to storing your secret in plaintext.
serve binds 127.0.0.1 by default. Binding elsewhere with --host turns on bearer-token gating for POST /_shutdown; the token is written to ~/.bkn/shutdown.token.
bkn never retries a failed operation for you. Errors carry a 'recoverable' flag and you decide.
Collections are created on first write. A typo in a namespace makes a new empty collection rather than an error - check 'bkn store collections' if a read comes back empty.

BKN_ENCRYPTION_KEY always stamps keyId 'v1' - the format the Node backend wrote. Two different single keys therefore both claim v1, and 'kv rekey' cannot tell them apart. Use BKN_ENCRYPTION_KEYS with distinct ids as soon as you have more than one key.
Ids are ULIDs and sort by creation time, including within one millisecond. Ordering by id is stable; ordering by a document field is not - store list orders by updated_at, then id.
A script must define main(input). A bare top-level expression is not the result and is never called.
There is no event loop in the script runtime: no promises, no async/await, no setTimeout. bkn.http.fetch blocks and returns its response directly.
A script with an empty allow_net has no network at all. Grant hosts explicitly, one script at a time.

Outbound requests that resolve to a loopback, link-local or private address are refused even when the hostname is allow-listed - that is what stops an allow-listed name from reaching the cloud metadata endpoint. BKN_SCRIPT_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NET=1 lifts it deliberately.
Every run is bounded by timeout_ms (default 5000). The bound cannot be removed, only raised, because an unbounded script wedges the daemon.
script update only changes the flags you actually pass, so editing the code never silently resets a timeout or an allowlist.

An access token stays valid until it expires, even after a logout: revocation applies to refresh tokens. Resolve a token with 'auth me', which checks the live user record, rather than trusting its claims.
Refresh tokens are single-use. Every refresh or switch-org returns a new one and kills the old; keep the newest.
A platform admin role does NOT grant any organization role. Operating the deployment and owning a tenant are separate things.
Changing a password or disabling a user revokes that user's sessions immediately.

The token signing secret is generated on first use and kept in kv (encrypted when a keyring exists). Set BKN_AUTH_SECRET to share one across instances; rotating it invalidates every outstanding access token.
Passwords passed as --password are visible in the process table. Use --password-stdin for anything real.
Scripts are operator code, not tenant code: bkn.auth.issue can mint a session for any user. Review a script the way you would review core.
